markerIdentity: Independent blind marker A (/root/a2_blind_a), round v1
independenceStatement: I read only the clean packet /tmp/skillpilot-a2/k4-blind-v1. I did not inspect repository/canonical content, author expectations, prior versions, another marker response, or reconciliation. All marks below are my independent judgement of the supplied synthetic submissions; these are not learner results.

decision.clarity: Task clear; two scoring interpretations require clarification.
decision.chatFeasibility: Feasible entirely in coach chat when the learner attaches an actual legible paper or digital drawing with its own ruler/grid scale. No Cockpit step is required by the task.
decision.goalSufficiency: The task prompts the candidate description's velocity-arrow performances. The current scoring, however, permits a pass without any explanation why the tip is not a position/contact; S05 is the concrete counterexample. I therefore do not accept the current pass claim as sufficient evidence of the whole stated goal.
decision.fourProtectedPerformances: A, B, C and D each carry 3/12 points. A score of zero on any whole performance limits the total to 9, so all four whole performances have protected weight. This protection does not guarantee that D's semantic explanation is demonstrated, because D(i) overlaps the drawing/scale evidence in C.
decision.noExtraGate: All pass decisions below use total >= 10 only.
decision.textOnlyCannotPass: Without any drawing A <= 1, B <= 1, C <= 1.5 and D <= 3; maximum 6.5/12. S13 shows this limit.
decision.coverageLimit: This judgement concerns the narrow stated velocity-arrow task. The packet does not supply the teaching goal text identified only by requiresAndCoversOnly, so no broader transfer claim about forces, fields, or all directed quantities is independently established.

findings.finding: D(i) can be evidenced by the actual correct shortened drawing plus the 6/3 = 2 cm working, under the global instruction to credit evidence anywhere and D(i)'s allowance for equivalent working. Thus S05 earns D=1 and passes 10/12 despite providing no semantic tip explanation at all. The claim that the learner can explain why the tip is no position/contact is then unestablished.
findings.scoringDecision: Credit the demonstrated geometric prediction; do not invent D(ii) or D(iii). S05: A3 B3 C3 D1 = 10, pass. S03 likewise 10; S04 9.5 because of its independent unit slip.
findings.minimalProposedRepair: State explicitly whether an accurately placed drawn tip together with its length working satisfies D(i), so a prose-only requirement is not silently added. Then reduce D(i) to 0.5 and allocate its remaining 0.5 to D(ii), keeping D total 3 and the sole total threshold at 10. S05 then cannot pass solely on the geometric overlap. Recheck the revised boundary cases independently.

findings.finding: The explicit requirement for an identifiable arrowhead conflicts at its boundary with the broad at-most-0.5 rule for isolated drawing slips. A completely absent arrowhead is also missing required visual evidence; the rubric only expressly classifies a misplaced arrowhead as a minor slip.
findings.scoringDecision: I apply the specific identifiable-arrowhead requirement: B(ii) has no visual directional evidence, so B=2, not 2.5. There is no additional penalty. The pass result remains 11/12 either way.
findings.minimalProposedRepair: Add one sentence: A missing arrowhead is missing drawing evidence and loses that sketch's 1 direction point; a single recognisable but reversed arrowhead can qualify for the 0.5 slip rule. Alternatively expressly include a demonstrably accidental missing head in the slip rule and adjust S16 consistently.

findings.finding: The maintained-misconception clauses clearly distinguish these cases from local slips. Correct copied statements elsewhere do not cancel an expressly maintained contrary claim. S12 explicitly retracts its earlier contact belief and therefore retains D. S17-S19 also contain visible/prose contradictions; I localise the stated misconception to A/B/C respectively and follow the rule against charging its consequences again.

The common slip policy supports one 0.5 loss at its origin for the isolated wrong final unit, arithmetic slip with its consistent 2.5-cm drawing, or repeated m-for-m/s legend slip with otherwise explicit conceptual distinction. No second loss for the same propagated error is justified.

The numerical physics is correct: 3 cm at 2 m/s per cm is 6 m/s; changing only arrow scale to 3 m/s per cm gives 2 cm and leaves a 1-cm drawn gap. A stationary-ground frame is specified. The apparent initial coincidence is explicitly a diagnostic counterexample, not an assertion of physical contact. Arithmetic and drawing demands are reasonable for the stated lower-stage placement after instruction. The drawing requirement is genuine and cannot be evaded by the complete text-only S13.

inspection.method: Every referenced PNG was individually opened with tools.view_image and visually examined as an actual image. I used the pictured ruler, not display centimetres or filenames, to judge origins, heads, lengths, scales and coincidence. Text and drawings were then considered together separately for each language.
